identification.summary: Sefid Flood is a Microsoft-named Iran-linked influence actor described in Microsoft Threat Analysis Center (MTAC) reporting on Iranian efforts around the 2024 US election [S1][S2]. Microsoft said it began staging for influence operations after the Iranian New Year in late March 2024 [S2][S3]. It specializes in impersonating social and political activist groups within a target audience [S2][S3].
identification.firstObserved: 2024-03 (Microsoft: preparing for influence operations since the Iranian New Year in late March 2024) [S2][S3]
identification.notes: Microsoft's report treats Sefid Flood as separate from the IRGC-run Mint Sandstorm (June 2024 spear-phishing of a presidential campaign official) and from the Storm-2035 covert news-site network [S2][S3]. No overlap with other vendors' cluster names was found in the sources gathered.

attribution.sponsor: Iran-linked, per Microsoft's description [S2][S3]. The sources gathered do not name a specific Iranian organization behind Sefid Flood.
attribution.basis: Microsoft MTAC reporting (August 2024), as relayed by secondary coverage [S2][S3][S4]. The Microsoft PDF could not be opened directly in this session [S1].

objectives: Per Microsoft, to stoke chaos, undermine trust in authorities and sow doubt about election integrity by impersonating activist groups [S2][S3].

sectors: Social and political activist groups (as impersonation cover and as potential targets of intimidation)
targeting.notes: Microsoft warned operations may go as far as intimidation, doxxing or violent incitement targeting political figures or social/political groups [S2][S3].

capabilities.summary: Influence tradecraft built on impersonating social and political activist groups in a target audience [S2][S3]. Microsoft said generative-AI use by actors in this reporting had limited impact so far, with many reverting to simpler techniques [S3]. No malware, intrusion tooling or infrastructure is attributed to Sefid Flood in the sources gathered.

campaigns.name: Staging for 2024 US election influence operations
campaigns.summary: Microsoft said Sefid Flood began preparing influence operations after the Iranian New Year in late March 2024, impersonating social and political activist groups to stoke chaos and undermine trust in authorities and election integrity [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: Microsoft MTAC public disclosure
campaigns.summary: Microsoft published its report on Iranian cyber-enabled influence operations targeting the 2024 US election, naming Sefid Flood alongside Mint Sandstorm and Storm-2035 and warning of possible escalation to intimidation, doxxing or violent incitement [S1][S2][S3][S4].

diamond.adversary: Iran-linked influence actor named by Microsoft; specific sponsoring organization not stated in sources gathered [S2][S3].
diamond.capability: Impersonation of social and political activist groups; possible escalation to intimidation, doxxing or violent incitement [S2][S3].
diamond.victim: US electorate and political figures or groups, 2024 election cycle [S2][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Undermine trust in authorities and election integrity in the United States [S2][S3].

gaps: Primary Microsoft MTAC report PDF could not be fetched (host unreachable); Sefid Flood details rely on secondary coverage of it. The Security Insider landing page fetched did not itself mention Sefid Flood [S1].
Sponsoring Iranian organization, confidence level, personas, platforms and infrastructure are not stated in sources gathered.
No activity after August 2024 was found; current status is unknown.
Whether Sefid Flood overlaps with other vendors' Iranian influence clusters is not established.
The Microsoft naming taxonomy entry (cited in the imported record) was not independently reviewed here.
